content.value_statement: Computer vision teams need practical guidance for models, data, inference, and deployment. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan production-ready vision workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides architecture planning for production computer vision systems.
Explains object detection optimization and model deployment workflows.
Covers performance, monitoring, reliability, and security considerations.
Provides starter CLI scripts for training, inference optimization, and dataset pipelines.
Lists common development, testing, deployment, and monitoring commands.
limitations: The included Python scripts are scaffolds and do not train real models.
No pretrained weights, datasets, or benchmark results are bundled.
Deployment commands require external infrastructure and project-specific configuration.
The references are broad guidance rather than a full implementation manual.

use_cases.title: Design a Vision Architecture
use_cases.description: Plan model serving, data flow, latency targets, monitoring, and reliability controls for a production vision service.

use_cases.title: Optimize Object Detection
use_cases.description: Review detection workflow choices, batching, caching, inference targets, and operational tradeoffs before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Deployment Readiness
use_cases.description: Create checklists for testing, container builds, Kubernetes rollout, observability, and incident response.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Vision Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main computer vision architecture choices for my image analysis project. Include model type, data needs, latency risks, and deployment concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Detection Optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my object detection pipeline plan and suggest improvements for accuracy, latency, batching, caching, and monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Create Deployment Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a production readiness checklist for a computer vision service using containers, Kubernetes, model monitoring, and rollback controls.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Vision System Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as a senior computer vision reviewer. Assess this design for scalability, privacy, model drift, observability, cost, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Plan a product defect detection service for a factory line.
output_examples.output: A concise architecture recommendation covering camera input, dataset labeling, detector selection, inference latency, monitoring, and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: Improve an object detection pipeline that misses small objects.
output_examples.output: A prioritized optimization plan covering image resolution, anchors or queries, augmentation, class imbalance, validation metrics, and inference cost.

output_examples.input: Prepare a deployment review for a vision API.
output_examples.output: A readiness checklist for tests, model versioning, container builds, Kubernetes deployment, logs, metrics, alerts, and rollback.

best_practices: Define accuracy, latency, throughput, and reliability targets before selecting models.
Validate datasets for quality, bias, privacy, and label consistency before training.
Monitor model drift, service health, and inference cost after deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not choose a large model before measuring latency and hardware limits.
Do not deploy vision systems without human review paths for low-confidence outputs.
Do not treat example deployment commands as complete production automation.

faq.question: Does this skill include a working vision model?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and starter script scaffolds, but it does not include trained weights or datasets.

faq.question: Can it help with object detection systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers object detection planning, optimization, deployment, and monitoring considerations.

faq.question: Does it support real-time inference planning?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes latency targets, batching, caching, load balancing, and throughput planning.

faq.question: Which tools are mentioned by the skill?
faq.answer: The documentation mentions Python, PyTorch, TensorFlow, OpenCV-related workflows, Docker, Kubernetes, and monitoring tools.

faq.question: Is this suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: It is best for users who understand machine learning basics and need production guidance.

faq.question: Can it replace a security or privacy review?
faq.answer: No. It can prompt for security considerations, but production systems still need project-specific review.
